newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil - HS barges hit highs, cargoes lag.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil - HS barges hit highs, cargoes lag.

text.p: Fuel oil gained on Wednesday, taking support from Iraqi tension bolstered by news of missile attacks on U.S. warplanes.
Rises were across the board, with the exception of well supplied Russian high sulphur straight-run and quietly demanded high sulphur cargoes.

High sulphur barges bounded $7 higher to hit post-Gulf War highs when $116 fob ARA was traded. Dealers said a combination of bullish news out of the Middle East and higher futures prices, fair bunker demand and a perceived tightness in the barge market were the main causes.
High sulphur cargoes were not so active, although a 20-25kt trade was done at mean cif NWE +25 cents for end-Sept delivery.

There was still some tightness in the market, although this was easier than some had previously thought. At least four of the six Portuguese tenders were seen accounted for and a number of NWE utilities were holding off.

Low sulpur cracked material saw a trader secure the Turkish 50kt buy tender at mean fob Med $9.50-10 cif Izmit, while a trader covered a short into the U.K. at $120 cif NWE for high viscosity material. There were several offers into the Med, one at $120 cif Italy, but none were taken up. -- +44 171 542 8980
